blocks.html:
READING PASSAGE 2

You should spend about 20 minutes on Questions 14–26, which are based on Reading Passage 2 below.

Roller coaster: the great fairground attraction

How they move

Like a passenger train, a roller coaster consists of a series of connected cars that move on a track. But unlike a passenger train, it has no engine or power source of its own. For most of the ride, it is moved only by the forces of inertia and gravity. The only exertion of energy occurs at the very beginning of the ride when the coaster train is pulled up the lift hill.

The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track. The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom. The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a motor. This turns the chain so that it continually moves up the hill like a long conveyor belt. The coaster cars grip onto the chain, which simply pulls them to the top. At the summit, the train is released and starts its descent.

The purpose of this initial ascent is to build up a sort of reservoir of potential energy, which simply means that as the coaster gets higher in the air, there is a greater distance gravity can pull it down.

As the train starts coasting down the hill, this potential energy is converted into kinetic energy (energy of motion), and the train speeds up. At the bottom of the hill, this has reached its maximum, and this propels the train up the second hill, again building up the potential-energy level.

In this way, the course of the track is constantly converting energy from kinetic to potential and back again. This fluctuation in acceleration is what makes roller coasters so much fun. At its most basic level, this is all a roller coaster is – a machine that uses gravity and inertia to send a train along a winding track.

Coasting through history

Roller coasters have a long, fascinating history. Their direct ancestors were ice slides, popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries. They consisted of a long, steep, wooden slide covered in ice. Riders walked up a ladder or set of stairs to the top of the slide, as high as 21 metres up. At the top, they climbed into sleds made of wood or blocks of ice and shot down the slope. At the base, the sleds would crash-land in a sand pile.

It seems that the idea was then imported into France. For most of the year, the warmer climate would melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead. To help the sleds move down these slides, they added wheels, and in 1817, for the first time, a train was attached to the track. The French continued to expand on this idea, coming up with more complex track layouts, with multiple cars and all sorts of twists and turns.

The first American roller coaster was built in the mountains of Pennsylvania in the mid-1800s, originally to provide an easy way to send coal to the railway 29 km down the mountain. When the track was first built, a crew at the bottom of the mountain would attach the cart to a team of mules after emptying the load, and the mules would drag it back up to the top. They were eventually replaced with steam engines to make the system more efficient.

Soon after these improvements were made, the railway company built a new tunnel that brought the freight trains much closer to the coal mine. No longer required for its original purpose, the roller coaster was configured as a 'scenic tour'. For one dollar, tourists got a leisurely ride up to the top of the mountain, followed by a wild, bumpy ride straight down. This was soon a resounding success, attracting thousands of tourists every year.

Scenic rides like this continued to thrive and were joined by wooden roller coasters similar to the ones we know today. These coasters were the main attraction at popular amusement parks throughout the United States, such as the many parks of Coney Island in New York. By the 1920s, roller coasters were in full swing, with some 2,000 rides in operation around the country.

Following the Great Depression, a decline in roller-coaster production began in the early 1930s, but a second roller-coaster boom in the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s revitalised the amusement-park industry and introduced a slew of innovative tubular steel coasters.

This was followed by a decline in interest for the rest of the decade, but since the early 1990s the amusement-park industry has experienced another coaster boom of sorts. New launching techniques and other technological developments have opened up a world of options for designers, so in some rides you feel as if you are flying. In the next few years we can expect to see many faster, taller and more twisted rides popping up in amusement parks around the world.

passageNotes.label: Paragraph A
passageNotes.text: 和客运列车一样，过山车由一系列相连的车厢组成，沿轨道运行。但与客运列车不同的是，它没有自身的发动机或动力源。在运行的大部分时间里，它仅靠惯性和重力驱动。唯一消耗能量的环节出现在行程最开始——过山车被拉升至最高坡。传统的提升装置是一条沿坡道铺设的长链，链条首尾相连形成环状，绕过坡顶和坡底的两个齿轮。坡底的齿轮由电机驱动，带动链条像传送带一样不断向上运行。过山车车厢扣住链条，被直接拉到顶端。到达最高点后，车厢脱钩释放，开始下冲。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph B
passageNotes.text: 初始爬坡的目的是积累一种势能储备，简单来说，过山车升得越高，重力能将其下拉的距离就越长。当车厢开始下滑时，势能转化为动能（运动能量），车厢随之加速。到达坡底时，动能达到最大值，推动车厢冲上第二个坡道，再次积累势能。如此循环，轨道不断将动能与势能相互转换。正是这种加速度的起伏变化，让过山车如此令人着迷。

passageNotes.label: Paragraph C
passageNotes.text: 现代过山车源自16世纪俄罗斯的冰面滑梯。在法国，由于气温较高，滑梯表面涂蜡，并在车厢上加装轮子以方便下滑。美国第一座过山车原本用于将煤炭从山上运下，最初由骡子牵引，后来改用蒸汽机提供动力。

items.text:
（1）题目 14：________
题目翻译：图中第14处所指的、沿坡道向上运行的提升部件是什么？
答案：chain
定位：“How they move”小节第2段，首句
原文：The traditional lifting mechanism is a long length of chain running up the hill under the track.
译文：传统的提升装置是一条长链条，在轨道下方向山坡上方运行。

解析：指线落在由许多环节组成的传动部件上；原文把传统提升装置明确称为 chain，因此填 chain。

（2）题目 15：________
题目翻译：图中第15处所指的带齿转动部件是什么？
答案：gear
定位：“How they move”小节第2段，第2句
原文：The chain is fastened in a loop, which is wound around a gear at the top of the hill and another one at the bottom.
译文：链条连接成环，绕在坡顶和坡底各一个齿轮上。

解析：原文说链条绕在坡顶和坡底的 gear 上，图中指线也落在齿轮位置，因此填 gear。

（3）题目 16：________
题目翻译：图中第16处所指的驱动装置是什么？
答案：motor
定位：“How they move”小节第2段，第3句
原文：The gear at the bottom of the hill is turned by a motor.
译文：坡底的齿轮由一台电动机带动。

解析：原文明确说坡底的齿轮由 motor 带动，对应图中的大型驱动部件，因此填 motor。

items.text:
（1）题目 17：Modern roller coasters are descended from 16th-century Russian slides with a surface of ________.
题目翻译：现代过山车源自16世纪俄罗斯滑道，其表面覆盖着什么？
答案：ice
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第1段，第2—3句
原文：Their direct ancestors were ice slides, popular in Russia in the 16th and 17th centuries. They consisted of a long, steep, wooden slide covered in ice.
译文：过山车的直接祖先是16、17世纪流行于俄罗斯的冰滑道；它由覆盖着冰面的长而陡的木制滑道构成。

解析：题干的 surface 对应原文 wooden slide covered in ice，因此填 ice。

（2）题目 18：In France, because of the higher temperatures, the wooden surface on the slides was ________, and ________ were attached to the cars to ease the descent.
题目翻译：在法国，较高气温下木制滑道表面经过怎样的处理？
答案：waxed
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第2段，第2句
原文：For most of the year, the warmer climate would melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead.
译文：一年中大部分时间，较温暖的气候会使冰融化，因此法国人改为建造涂蜡的滑道。

解析：原文说冰会融化，所以法国人改建 waxed slides；空格位于 was 后，需要形容处理状态的 waxed。

（3）题目 19：In France, because of the higher temperatures, the wooden surface on the slides was ________, and ________ were attached to the cars to ease the descent.
题目翻译：为了便于下滑，车上加装了什么？
答案：wheels
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第2段，第3句
原文：To help the sleds move down these slides, they added wheels, and in 1817, for the first time, a train was attached to the track.
译文：为了帮助雪橇沿滑道下行，他们加装了轮子；1817年，列车首次被连接到轨道上。

解析：原文直接说 they added wheels，与题干 were attached to the cars 对应，因此填复数 wheels。

（4）题目 20：The first US roller coaster was used for transporting ________ down a mountainside in carts.
题目翻译：美国第一座过山车最初用来运送什么？
答案：coal
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第3段，首句
原文：The first American roller coaster was built in the mountains of Pennsylvania in the mid-1800s, originally to provide an easy way to send coal to the railway 29 km down the mountain.
译文：美国第一座过山车于19世纪中期建在宾夕法尼亚山区，最初是为了方便把煤运到山下29公里处的铁路。

解析：原文说它最初用于把 coal 运送到山下铁路，因此填 coal。

（5）题目 21：Initially, these were pulled by mules, but in time power was produced by ________.
题目翻译：取代骡子并提供动力的是什么？
答案：steam engines
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第3段，末句
原文：They were eventually replaced with steam engines to make the system more efficient.
译文：后来骡子最终被蒸汽机取代，使运输系统更加高效。

解析：原文完整词组是 steam engines，因此规范答案为 steam engines；题干已经表达提供动力的语义。题干已明确动力来源时，省略修饰语 steam 后的 engines 仍语法完整并指向同一对象。

items.text:
（1）题目 22：The earliest modifications to the basic slide were made in France.
题目翻译：对基础滑道最早的改进是在法国完成的。
答案：TRUE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第2段
原文：For most of the year, the warmer climate would melt the ice, so the French started building waxed slides instead. To help the sleds move down these slides, they added wheels, and in 1817, for the first time, a train was attached to the track.
译文：法国人因气候较暖而改用涂蜡滑道，随后加装轮子，并在1817年首次把列车连接到轨道上。

解析：原文先介绍俄罗斯的基本冰滑道，随后说法国人改用涂蜡滑道、加装轮子并首次把列车连接到轨道上，明确构成最早的改进，因此答案为 TRUE。

（2）题目 23：Roller coasters continued to increase in popularity throughout the 1920s and 1930s.
题目翻译：在整个20世纪20年代和30年代，过山车的受欢迎程度持续上升。
答案：FALSE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第6段，首句
原文：Following the Great Depression, a decline in roller-coaster production began in the early 1930s
译文：大萧条之后，过山车产量从20世纪30年代初开始下降。

解析：原文说20年代蓬勃发展，但30年代初产量开始下降；“整个两年代持续上升”与原文相反，因此答案为 FALSE。

（3）题目 24：New roller-coaster technology was introduced in the 1970s in response to public demand.
题目翻译：20世纪70年代引入新的过山车技术，是为了响应公众需求。
答案：NOT GIVEN
定位：“Coasting through history”小节第6段
原文：a second roller-coaster boom in the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s revitalised the amusement-park industry and introduced a slew of innovative tubular steel coasters.
译文：20世纪70年代及80年代初的第二次过山车热潮重振了游乐园行业，并带来大量创新的管状钢制过山车。

解析：原文说明70年代热潮带来创新钢制过山车，却没有说明这是“响应公众需求”造成的；该因果关系未给出，因此答案为 NOT GIVEN。

（4）题目 25：Roller coasters were less popular for most of the 1980s than in the 1970s and 1990s.
题目翻译：在20世纪80年代的大部分时间里，过山车不如70年代和90年代受欢迎。
答案：TRUE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节末段，首句
原文：This was followed by a decline in interest for the rest of the decade, but since the early 1990s the amusement-park industry has experienced another coaster boom of sorts.
译文：此后在80年代余下时间里，人们的兴趣下降；但从90年代初起，游乐园行业又经历了一轮过山车热潮。

解析：原文说80年代初热潮之后，该年代余下时间兴趣下降，而90年代初又出现热潮，与题干一致，因此答案为 TRUE。

（5）题目 26：The design of roller-coaster rides became more varied in the 1990s.
题目翻译：20世纪90年代，过山车项目的设计变得更加多样。
答案：TRUE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节末段，第2句
原文：New launching techniques and other technological developments have opened up a world of options for designers, so in some rides you feel as if you are flying.
译文：新的发射技术和其他技术发展为设计师提供了丰富选择，有些项目甚至让乘客感觉像在飞行。

解析：原文说新发射技术和其他发展为设计师打开了丰富选择，直接支持“设计更加多样”，因此答案为 TRUE。

原文：a second roller-coaster boom in the 1970s and the beginning of the 1980s revitalised the amusement-park industry and introduced a slew of innovative tubular steel coasters.
译文：20世纪70年代及80年代初的第二次过山车热潮重振了游乐园行业，并带来大量创新的管状钢制过山车。

解析：原文说明70年代热潮带来创新钢制过山车，却没有说明这是“响应公众需求”造成的；该因果关系未给出，因此答案为 NOT GIVEN。

（4）题目 25：Roller coasters were less popular for most of the 1980s than in the 1970s and 1990s.
题目翻译：在20世纪80年代的大部分时间里，过山车不如70年代和90年代受欢迎。
答案：TRUE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节末段，首句
原文：This was followed by a decline in interest for the rest of the decade, but since the early 1990s the amusement-park industry has experienced another coaster boom of sorts.
译文：此后在80年代余下时间里，人们的兴趣下降；但从90年代初起，游乐园行业又经历了一轮过山车热潮。

解析：原文说80年代初热潮之后，该年代余下时间兴趣下降，而90年代初又出现热潮，与题干一致，因此答案为 TRUE。

（5）题目 26：The design of roller-coaster rides became more varied in the 1990s.
题目翻译：20世纪90年代，过山车项目的设计变得更加多样。
答案：TRUE
定位：“Coasting through history”小节末段，第2句
原文：New launching techniques and other technological developments have opened up a world of options for designers, so in some rides you feel as if you are flying.
译文：新的发射技术和其他技术发展为设计师提供了丰富选择，有些项目甚至让乘客感觉像在飞行。

解析：原文说新发射技术和其他发展为设计师打开了丰富选择，直接支持“设计更加多样”，因此答案为 TRUE。
